correctness.rationale: For m>=2, 1<=k<2m, all μ>=0, t>0, every follower set has pair orbit (r,s). A strict r->r+1 exchange replaces a singleton by the mate of another: A1=A0+E_uv+E_vu. Interpolation stays positive definite, -Aθ is Metzler with positive uv link for θ<1, so derivative of trace exp(-tAθ) equals -2t(exp(-tAθ))_uv<0. Finite iteration proves all orbits ordered and every equality case. Gamma integral for all p>0 and finite-horizon integration are valid by positive eigenvalues and positive integrands; eigenvalues follow pair-mode decomposition and 2x2 quotient. Package verify.py passed 7401 checks including exact small-size charpolys. Finite tests alone are not proof.

originality.rationale: The complete earlier balanced-multipartite all-budget theorem covers the first-inverse unscreened grouping for at least three matching pairs as a special case, which is expressly excluded from novelty. Its actual theorem and rational proof do not imply the pointwise heat-trace ordering. The new strict comparison across every positive time and all competitor pair-count orbits implies all finite-horizon objectives and positive inverse powers, not conversely from a single inverse moment. Focal general 2013 leader-selection and 2014 joint-centrality/path work do not state this theorem; remaining priority risk is unindexed equivalent work.

value.rationale: A pre-existing leader classification for one inverse moment does not imply uniform finite-horizon noise-response optimality. The new all-time strict heat-trace comparison solves every positive time, screening and positive inverse spectral order simultaneously, and classifies/ranks all follower-pair orbits with explicit spectra and counts. This provides robust time-scale independent intervention choices for dense graphs with a failed perfect matching, not a mere parameter renaming of the known p=1 result.
